generationSummary: Reward and penalty audit logging tests verify that the system creates, stores, and provides controlled access to audit logs for all loyalty point adjustments (rewards and penalties). Tests cover audit log creation on reward/penalty events, secure storage, administrative review access, traceability preservation, and privacy-aware user identification handling. resolvedExceptions: User-identifying values in raw adjustment logs may require controlled lookup path for authorized reviewers rather than direct exposure in stored log entries
resolutionNotes: R100b targets audit logging specifically for rewards and penalties. PRIMARY evidence establishes that adjustment audit logging must preserve traceability (E1, E7), support controlled review (E1), remain compatible with privacy expectations (E1), and follow standard audit log integrity and content requirements (E8, E13). E5 and E10 indicate implementation of broader user activity and audit logging that encompasses reward/penalty adjustments. E9 notes that the reward formula is not yet finalized. The key tension is between user-linked traceability requirements and privacy constraints around direct user identification in logs (E1, E5), which should be treated as an exception/design consideration rather than a blocking gap. Standard audit log protections (no modification, no unauthorized deletion, secure storage, administrative review access) apply per E8 and E13.
